_purpose: The last-trained-SHA bookmark per repo, per training round. Without this we cannot compute 'what changed since Taey last learned' — which is the prerequisite for the mandatory diff/changelog refresh cadence. Update on EVERY completed training round.
_why_it_matters: Taey's load-bearing capability is being the custodian who knows what exists (what is canonical, what is dead code, what the proven path is). That capability DECAYS with every commit. Measured 2026-07-21: 221 commits of drift since ep3's corpus snapshot, with zero mechanism to detect it.

drift_refined_2026-07-21._why: Clarity (round-2) challenged the raw commit count: 'commit count alone doesn't tell you whether those commits touch capability surfaces — I'd want the git log + touched-file diff before that drives a mandatory-cadence rule.' Correct challenge; measured properly here.
drift_refined_2026-07-21.finding: Drift is CONCENTRATED, not uniform. apply-machine = 106 of 150 code-touching commits (71%) and is the system Taey must operate. treasurer's apparent 58-commit drift was mostly DOCS (only 10 code). The earlier flat '221 commits' framing implied even churn and was misleading.
drift_refined_2026-07-21.supersedes: drift_measured_2026-07-21 (raw commit counts) — retained above for the record, but do NOT drive cadence from it.
drift_refined_2026-07-21.remaining_proxy_caveat: 'code-touching' is still a PROXY for capability-surface change: a .py commit may be a typo or a lint fix. The real measure needs diff size / API-signature analysis. Not yet done — do not present this as capability drift.
drift_refined_2026-07-21.note: palios-training rose 39->48 during 2026-07-21 because tutor committed throughout the session.

capability_surface_measured.finding: 62 of 117 commits (53%) moved a function/class SIGNATURE in 6 days on the system Taey must operate. This is genuine capability-surface drift, not typo churn — it upgrades the earlier 'code-touching' proxy to a real measure.
capability_surface_measured.implication: Weights trained on last week's signatures are ALREADY wrong. You cannot train on a cadence fast enough to track 62 signature changes/6 days. This is direct evidence FOR the lanes' retrieval-at-HEAD recommendation over train-on-diffs — retrieval is not the cheap compromise, it is the only mechanism that keeps pace.
capability_surface_measured.instrument_note: My FIRST attempt at this measurement was broken — it reported 0 signature-changing commits across 12,870 changed lines, which is implausible on its face. A direct cross-check found 776 def/class diff lines, proving the script (malformed `git show` pathspec), not the repo, was wrong. Re-measured with a simple per-commit loop. Recorded because an implausible measurement must be challenged, not published.
